entities.summary:
Peugeot, a prominent French automotive brand, traces its origins to the early 19th century when it was established on September 26, 1810, in Poissy, France. As part of the Stellantis group, Peugeot has become a significant player in the global automotive industry, contributing to the evolution of transportation and manufacturing practices in Western Europe. The company is named after the Peugeot family, particularly Jean-Pierre and his descendants, who were instrumental in its initial development and expansion. The brand symbolizes not only the growth of the automotive sector but also the broader technological advancements of the Industrial Revolution.

Throughout its history, Peugeot has achieved numerous milestones, including the production of its first car in 1889 and the introduction of the first mass-produced vehicle, the Peugeot 201, in 1929. The company has continuously adapted to changing market demands, showcasing innovations such as the invention of the 3D-printed car body and advancements in electric vehicle technology. By the mid-20th century, Peugeot had established itself as a household name, with production facilities across Europe and a reputation for quality and reliability. The brand's models, such as the Peugeot 205 and 508, have garnered international acclaim and have significantly influenced automotive design and engineering.
